title: Choose the visual world — davidsling.in landing
question: The roll dealt the Reservation Chart. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Each card also shows one of the three first-viewport leads you asked to see.

options.label: Reservation Chart
options.lineage: Indian Railways printed reservation charts and yellow station name boards
options.thesis: The site is the chart pasted beside the coach door: find the work by running a finger down it.
options.viewport: Lead = the work: a yellow trilingual name board (English, Malayalam, Kannada) over a full-width printed chart whose three rows are Wave, Equanim and Offlyn.
options.risk: Peers outside India may miss the reference; dot-matrix can drift techy; the Malayalam and Kannada must be verified by David.

raised.raise: Attention is the state system: every row and control has at-rest, approached, pressed and done states, and the finger-run highlight is the shared vocabulary.
Printed discipline: every tone is paper, ink or board yellow; no decorative tints or gradients.
The chart is live: rows print from real repo data at build time instead of being pictured.
Each column holds exactly one verifiable fact; nothing ornamental lives in the table.

options.label: Contact Sheet
options.lineage: photographers' contact sheets marked up with a red china marker
options.thesis: Taste is selection: every project is a strip of frames, and the red grease pencil circles the one that shipped.
options.viewport: Lead = you + one line: a strip of portrait frames from David's photo, one circled in red, a hand-marked line beside it; project strips start below the fold.
options.risk: The most familiar of the set: photo-editorial portfolios often land here, and it needs real frame imagery for every strip.

options.label: Cut-Paper Wit
options.thesis: Every project introduced by a visual pun cut from paper; the joke lands before the caption does.
options.viewport: Lead = a craft moment: a cut-paper pun built around David's cut-out photo that you can nudge, with a hand-lettered headline and obedient small type at the foot.
options.case: Wins both axes: the designer's-designer canon matches 'designer's eye' and David's irreverent voice, and each project gets an instant pun label (Wave as two speech bubbles, Equanim as a pendulum, Offlyn as a friends-of-friends Venn heart).
options.risk: The puns must genuinely land or it turns twee; it needs authored cut-paper art and ideally David's own handwriting.

options.label: Ma Arrangement
options.thesis: Three projects placed as primary, secondary and supporting lines, with the empty plaster doing as much work as the stems.
options.viewport: Lead = the work: Wave rises as the tall primary line, Equanim and Offlyn angle off it, each a live mini-artifact, with David's name set vertically off-centre.
options.case: Holds product clarity (three projects map to the three lines of an arrangement) but is weaker on identification: the cultural home isn't David's, and quiet can read corporate.
options.risk: Quiet restraint is the easiest version to make look like an agency site.

options.label: Luminescent Understory
options.thesis: Attention lights the path two steps ahead.
options.viewport: Near-black ground, projects as distant pulses that bloom on approach.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is the dark neon look David ruled out.
options.risk: Reads as the AI-era dark glow default.
options.kept: Attention as a state system, now on the assigned card.

options.label: Noir One-Sheet
options.thesis: A small figure throwing a huge shadow.
options.viewport: David's cut-out small, his shadow four times his size across the page.
options.case: Loses both axes: cream stock is a saturated AI tell and the film frame says nothing about the work.
options.kept: Two-ink discipline, now on the assigned card.

options.label: ASCII Live Render
options.thesis: The scene re-rendered live as type.
options.viewport: A glyph portrait of David on black.
options.case: Loses both axes: it is exactly the techy terminal look ruled out.
options.kept: Render the work live rather than picturing it, now on the assigned card.

options.label: Night Flight Six-Pack
options.thesis: Six calm dials, each owning one truth.
options.viewport: Projects as gauges on a black panel.
options.case: Loses both axes: dark, instrumented, and tool-costumed.
options.kept: One verifiable fact per element, now on the assigned card.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: The light personal portfolio, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Lead = you + one line: avatar with a name sticker, a centred two-tone headline, a pill button, and project cards with years below.
canonCard.risk: This is the bought-template look you said would feel wrong.
